title: Training Note — Autopay Drafts and the Preferred Employer Rate
content:
The preferred employer rate of an Apartment Home Lease is raised by an autopay step for the autopay drafts received on the lease in the last 12 months, counting lease payments made by ACH autopay dated after the same day of the month twelve months before the handling date: ten or more drafts raise it by 0.005, six to nine raise it by 0.0025, and fewer leave it unchanged.

## Questions answered

**Which payments count as drafts?** Lease payments on the Apartment Home Lease ledger whose instrument is ACH autopay. One-time bank transfers, card payments, money orders and cashier's checks are not autopay drafts.

**What are "the last 12 months"?** Payments dated after the same day of the month twelve months before the handling date, up to the handling date. With a handling date of 15 March 2026, a draft dated 16 March 2025 counts and one dated 15 March 2025 does not.

**What does the step do?** It raises the preferred employer rate itself; the raised rate is applied to the period's base rent line.

## Step table

| ACH autopay lease payments in the last 12 months | Autopay step added to the preferred employer rate |
|---|---|
| 10 or more | 0.005 (half a percentage point, 0.5%) |
| 6 to 9 | 0.0025 (a quarter of a percentage point, 0.25%) |
| 5 or fewer | nothing |

**Boundaries.** 9 drafts: 0.0025; 10 drafts: 0.005. 5 drafts: nothing; 6 drafts: 0.0025.

*Hypothetical:* on a floor plan rate of 0.03, eleven drafts in the window raise the rate to 0.035; seven drafts raise it to 0.0325.
